transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. I'm coming in today because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry and anxiety for a really long time now, for over two years. It feels like I'm always anxious about something and I just can't seem to turn it off.
Did your anxiety start after a specific stressful life event or major change, or has it been present even without one? If there was a stressor, what was it?
I can't really recall a specific stressful event or major life change that triggered it. It seems to have just been present and ongoing without any one clear cause.
Along with the worry, have you often had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, muscle tension, irritability, or sleep problems?

Yes, I definitely feel wound up and on edge all the time, my body feels incredibly stiff and tense, and I find myself getting really snappy and easily annoyed because worries constantly interrupt my focus. I'm not as sure about being easily tired or having specific sleep problems, but the restlessness, tension, and irritability are very prominent.
Over the past 6 months, have you felt worried or anxious more days than not?
Yes, I've been feeling anxious and worried almost every single day. It's actually been going on for much longer than just six months—it has been about two years and one month now.
How much is this anxiety affecting your daily life, like your work, relationships, or ability to handle everyday responsibilities?

It's having a massive impact because constant worries about my job and family finances keep intruding into my mind, making it incredibly hard to focus at work. On top of that, my patience is so low that I keep snapping at my family over minor things, which is really straining my relationships.
Do you think your anxiety could be related to a medical condition, or to using substances like caffeine, alcohol, drugs, or any medications?
No, I don't think it's related to any of those. I don't have any known medical issues, and I don't really drink much caffeine or alcohol, nor do I use any drugs or take medications.
Do you also get sudden attacks of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

No, I don't experience those sudden attacks of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath. Instead, it's just a constant, chronic state of worry and tension where I always feel on edge.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different areas of life, or is your anxiety mostly focused on just one specific issue?

Yes, I worry about almost everything rather than just one specific thing. My anxiety spreads across so many different areas, like my job performance, our family's finances, and my family's well-being. It really feels like there isn't a single part of my life that I'm not constantly anxious about.
